deliveryClassification.rationale: Owner decision OD-2026-10-08-CS6 places the existing authenticated route/session boundary in Release 1 implementation scope after its declared gates; no new route or dashboard surface is authorized.

problem: Candidate deep links and route navigation must share one session-rendering boundary so delayed, failed or unauthenticated session lookup never mounts private feature content or leaks a previous owner's cached data.
functionalRequirements: Next App Router route group (app)/layout.tsx wraps all current private routes with one AuthenticatedShell. Actual route files, not a separately invented routing map, are authoritative; dashboard-shell navigation maps to those real routes.

Session pending shows neutral Loading workspace; session lookup failure shows Workspace unavailable plus retry; unauthenticated success renders no private children and clears auth query cache before replacing route with /. These are existing behaviors to verify, not completed fresh test evidence.

Cold/untrusted delayed or failed session lookup must not mount private child components or send their owner-private queries; response HTML/RSC payload contains no fixture private data. Use fresh browser context/empty session cache for those cases. Authenticated cached navigation is a separate positive control, not incorrectly expected to become pending on refetch.

Shared query provider/session query survives private navigation. Logout and session-expired handling remain centralized; cache cleanup isolates successive owners. Do not redesign auth or claim client shell substitutes for API ownership enforcement.
CS-13/14/16/17/19 own their feature/content work; this routing boundary supplies composition without bundling those tickets' implementation or visual acceptance into CS-6.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: CROSS_MODULE. Existing app route-group layout composes AuthenticatedShell; useSession shares ['session']; ownerKey scopes private data. No global store, bespoke router, duplicate gate or new server auth system.

AC1 has no new API contract. Reuse the existing GET /api/session contract through useSession; the route group is a client composition boundary, not a new server authorization mechanism. Private APIs continue to enforce server-derived ownership.
persistence: NOT_APPLICABLE to new schema: client cache ownership and session-derived authorization are affected; no user/application database write is required by route decomposition.
apiContract: EXISTING_CONTRACT: GET /api/session is the existing endpoint consumed by the shell. Authenticated responses include authenticated, csrf, a stable hashed owner digest, email/phone and aiEnabled where configured; anonymous responses may include registrationEnabled and cognitoEnabled. It does not return a session identity field. The source design map's empty existingEndpoints list means no endpoint is introduced by CS-6. Private API routes independently enforce server session ownership. Do not expose provider tokens or accept client-supplied owner for route data.

problem: The ticket's source wording describes a V1/V2 cross-workspace boundary that no longer exists in the consolidated repository. Current code defines `MatchingProfile` in `packages/core/src/profile.ts`, matcher-owned `MatchableProfile` in `packages/shared/src/types.ts`, the consumer in `packages/matching/src/context.ts`, and the worker call in `apps/workers/search/src/collect.ts`. The remaining problem is to state this three-field contract in authoritative architecture documentation and retain a deterministic regression proof; the historical fabricated-field override is evidence of a past defect, not current behavior.
value: Preserving the existing minimal three-field application projection prevents future matcher changes from silently consuming absent or fabricated profile values. This specification separates already-present source behavior from the remaining documentation and mutation-proof work without claiming either has been completed.
desiredOutcome: The architecture record names the canonical root packages and accurately documents the current three-field application projection and call direction; an isolated planned regression demonstrates that adding a fourth-field read fails typechecking and that restoring the source returns the baseline to green. No runtime shape, scoring, API, or persistence behavior changes in this ticket.
inScope: Document and test the existing `MatchingProfile` to `MatchableProfile` compile-time boundary across the canonical root workspace. Preserve the `expectedCtc`, `yearsOfExperience`, and `willingToRelocate` projection and persisted per-search snapshot semantics.
functionalRequirements: The source title and portions of its evidence retain versioned-workspace wording from before the completed single-codebase consolidation. Treat those statements as historical provenance, not current architecture: active paths are `packages/core/src/profile.ts`, `packages/shared/src/types.ts`, `packages/matching/src/context.ts`, and `apps/workers/search/src/collect.ts`; no active `v2/` package tree exists.

Current code already narrows both application shapes to the same three fields and passes the MatchingProfile directly; source history records the prior fabricated-field override and its removal. Distinguish that existing evidence from the still-required architecture-record review and not-yet-run mutation proof; do not report the old failure mode as a currently reproduced runtime defect.

The compile-time contract is specifically the application subobject passed from `MatchingProfile` to `buildCandidateContext`: it exposes only `expectedCtc`, `yearsOfExperience`, and `willingToRelocate`. The matching consumer may not read a fourth application field unless the canonical snapshot contract is deliberately reviewed and updated.

`buildCandidateContext` has a separate optional `resumeText` parameter whose default is an empty string; the search worker currently calls `buildCandidateContext(profile)` without passing raw resume text. CS-78 specifies only the typed MatchingProfile/application boundary and does not claim to redesign or prove all resume-text handling elsewhere in the matching system.

Preserve the deliberately minimal snapshot created by `matchingProfile`; do not pass or serialize `currentCtc`, `noticePeriodDays`, or the full writable `ApplicationDetails` into matching to silence a type error.

At the search-worker call site, pass the typed `MatchingProfile` directly to the matcher. Do not add `as MatchableProfile`, `as any`, fabricated fallback fields, or a second projection that changes scoring inputs.

Reconcile historical V1/V2 names and paths in the source acceptance criteria against the current one-workspace architecture: document `packages/core`, `packages/shared`, `packages/matching`, and `apps/workers/search` as the active boundary; do not reintroduce versioned workspaces or file dependencies as an implementation requirement.

A mutation proving the boundary must be isolated from the developer checkout: make `packages/matching/src/context.ts` read a fourth application property absent from `MatchableProfile`, require the canonical typecheck to fail with the property diagnostic at the consumer, restore the mutation, and require the same typecheck to pass. Record both outcomes; a pass-only run is insufficient.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: CROSS_MODULE and DATA_MODEL. `packages/core/src/profile.ts` defines `MatchingProfile` and `matchingProfile()` projects the stored writable profile into the minimal per-search snapshot; `packages/shared/src/types.ts` defines the matcher-owned `MatchableProfile`; `packages/matching/src/context.ts` consumes it; `apps/workers/search/src/collect.ts` passes the snapshot to the matcher. This is a data contract, not JavaScript runtime immutability (`Object.freeze`). Keep this direction and the structural TypeScript boundary; do not add an API, service, endpoint, or new persistence field.

Current `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` generically describes profile projection but does not yet spell out the canonical source paths and exact three application fields. The documentation acceptance remains a real gap: name the active paths, list the projection fields, and describe call direction; do not repeat historical V1/V2 terminology as current architecture.
persistence: The existing `search_runs.matching_profile` snapshot remains the persisted source for a search run; this ticket must not widen its application projection or change schema, nullability, indexes, migrations, retention, or replay semantics. Inspect `packages/core/src/schema.ts` and the `createSearch` implementation before any later implementation change.

Require-ci requests ci.yml runs filtered by the resolved SHA. PASS requires legible completed-success evidence; failed/cancelled/timed-out/malformed/inconsistent payloads refuse, queued/in-progress/absent evidence waits only within the configured deadline then refuses. Older success cannot override a newer failure.

Downstream verify/shipping jobs cannot execute when require-ci refuses. problem: The verification domain requires an explicit candidate-owned state machine and separate privileged review boundary. Current runtime does not prove this domain exists, so the specification must define a future contract without presenting it as deployed.
functionalRequirements: Model only the approved transitions UNVERIFIED -> PENDING -> IN_REVIEW, then IN_REVIEW -> VERIFIED|NEEDS_INFO|REJECTED; an authorized candidate may resubmit NEEDS_INFO or REJECTED through an explicit revision/idempotency-fenced path back to PENDING, and an authorized reviewer may explicitly revoke VERIFIED. Reject every other transition server-side.

Candidate edits may submit evidence but can never assign VERIFIED or reviewer identity. Reviewer identity, decision reason and timestamps are server-derived and every privileged decision produces a redacted audit event.

Profile photo remains optional for ordinary candidate profile use; when a candidate supplies one as verification evidence, accept only JPEG or PNG up to the existing 5 MiB storage bound, strip metadata before private encrypted publication, reject malformed/oversized files with typed errors and never expose a public URL. Notes and call metadata remain restricted, no call recording is collected by default, raw content follows purpose-based deletion and only minimal audit provenance may remain.

The future API contract must return safe denial for unauthenticated, wrong-owner and non-privileged actors, prevent replay/stale-revision writes, and preserve the candidate's current state on validation or storage failure.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: DATA_MODEL / API_CONTRACT / AUTH_IDENTITY. apiContract: PLANNED_CONTRACT (not an existing route): GET /api/verification returns only the authenticated candidate's status/revision/nextAction; POST /api/verification/evidence accepts multipart photo plus client idempotency key and current revision; POST /api/admin/verifications/:verificationId/decision accepts `{decision: VERIFIED|NEEDS_INFO|REJECTED, reason}` only for the existing CS-40 server-enforced verification-review capability. Candidate routes require session+CSRF and owner-derived identity; reviewer route requires server RBAC and never grants generic database access. Define deterministic 401 unauthenticated, 403 wrong actor/role, 404 non-disclosing unknown ID, 409 stale revision/duplicate conflict, 413 size, 415 type, 422 validation and 507 capacity errors; success returns the new state/revision and never tokens or raw private evidence. These routes are planned contracts, not current implementation.
persistence: PLANNED_DATA: verification record belongs to one candidate and stores state, revision, server timestamps, reviewer digest and authorized reason, plus an evidence reference; supplied photo bytes use the existing encrypted private-storage pattern, JPEG/PNG allowlist, 5 MiB bound and metadata stripping. Raw photo/notes/call metadata are deleted when no longer required by the candidate-owned verification purpose; minimal non-sensitive transition provenance may remain for audit integrity. No numeric retention period is invented; any statutory/product duration remains a later explicit legal/product decision. Add legal transition checks, owner indexes and reversible migration/rollback; do not claim these tables exist today.

problem: The authenticated route group composes one shared shell, but source-level structure and an approved expanded-dashboard reference do not prove parity, secure cold-session rendering or responsive behavior across the dashboard/jobs/applications shell.
value: Give authenticated candidates a consistent shell while ensuring private content is rendered only after the server session confirms authentication.
functionalRequirements: Authenticated actor is the candidate whose identity is derived by the existing session API. `apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx` is the shared route boundary and `AuthenticatedShell` is the session gate; do not render child workspace content while session is pending, errored, expired or unauthenticated. Compare expanded/collapsed shell geometry against the exact dashboard expanded and jobs expanded/collapsed canonical references. Page content uses actual API-backed state or explicit pending/empty/error/unavailable state. Do not copy sample candidate name, jobs, counts, match scores or application data from board images. If no API data is available, shell may render only non-sensitive navigation and a safe state.

Cold session, API session error, unauthorized response, expired session and stale-revision page state each have a distinct safe expected result: no private child render before auth; retry only for recoverable session/network failure; redirect signed-out on session expiry; route-level conflict behavior belongs to the current data feature and must not be swallowed by the shell.
Private workspace metadata stays noindex; no session identity or personal data is inserted into title, description, Open Graph, static build output or client-readable persistence.

apiContract: EXISTING_CONTRACT: authenticated shell consumes GET `/api/session` via the existing session client; API derives owner from opaque session cookie. persistence: No new persistence. Sidebar open/closed may remain in-memory unless an existing approved preference contract specifies otherwise; never store credentials, session identifier or candidate content in browser storage.
accessibility: Sidebar control has an accessible name and `aria-expanded` reflecting actual state; nav is a labelled landmark; active destination uses current-page semantics; menu/links work with keyboard, visible focus, logical order and escape/close behavior for mobile drawer. Session loading/error/expiry announcements are perceivable; preserve focus on redirects and avoid background focus into hidden content.
responsive: Use approved expanded/collapsed desktop references, then reflow to the approved mobile navigation without horizontal page overflow at 320/390/768/1024/1280/1440px. Sidebar collapse is not the sole mobile interaction; touch targets and focus order remain usable.

Complete manual design and screen-reader review; reconcile docs and evidence against the exact reviewed implementation SHA.

Apply supplied desktop/mobile reference to only the supported email signup and verification states; obtain an outage-state design before implementing that unresolved presentation.
Implement labeled form/error/status/focus behavior and privacy-safe redirects; do not store OTP/token/code in browser state.
Add component/API mock tests for success, invalid/expired state, provider-disabled and unavailable server responses; add Chromium/Firefox/WebKit keyboard and responsive browser cases.
Complete axe checks and manual screen-reader/design review; use disposable Cognito acceptance only after external configuration is authorized.

definitionOfDone: Implementation DoD: approved email-first session/provider contract; exact supported state matrix; design review of supplied auth references plus approved outage state; no token/code/OTP persistence/rendering; labeled keyboard flow and announcements; component/API and Chromium/Firefox/WebKit tests pass; accessibility automation and human screen-reader acceptance recorded; successful callback is confirmed by GET `/api/session` and workspace navigation; errors remain signed out. Release DoD additionally requires disposable hosted Cognito OTP acceptance and exact-SHA CI. No provider setup or product implementation is claimed by this specification.

problem: There is no verified sender/SES/Cognito template evidence. The approved owner record only targets a verified CareerScope domain identity; it does not choose a concrete From/Reply-To address, locale set, visual treatment, expiry duration, DNS records or SES production-access state.
value: Provide trustworthy, abuse-resistant email verification messages only after sender ownership, template correctness, delivery controls and real disposable-account delivery are evidenced.
functionalRequirements: Owner decision provenance: `docs/OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-02.md#CS-90..CS-94` approves a verified CareerScope domain identity as the sender target; exact From/Reply-To addresses, supported locales and template visual acceptance remain undecided. Do not guess addresses, translate copy, claim a verified sender or copy illustrative design content.

For the current email-code flow, the Cognito verification template must contain the provider's required `{####}` code placeholder. Signup/attribute-verification code validity follows Cognito's provider-defined verification window (AWS currently documents 24 hours for verification codes); do not describe that as an arbitrary pool-configured duration. Authentication/MFA challenge expiry is a separate provider/configuration concern and must not be copied into verification-email wording. Do not use a verification link template in place of email OTP without an explicit product decision.

Cognito `VerificationMessageTemplateType` provides one `EmailMessage` body plus subject/code fields, not independently configured multipart HTML and text MIME bodies. Specify accessible, text-readable content and any provider-supported rendering only; do not promise dual-body delivery. When using a custom Cognito/SES message, require `DEVELOPER` sending mode, the provider's subject/body/placeholder limits and the selected message-type contract before activation. Content may contain only approved product name, concise security guidance, the required code placeholder, provider-authoritative expiry wording and owner-approved support route. Do not include passwords, access/refresh tokens, authorization codes, raw profile fields, candidate data or unnecessary recipient identifiers; do not load remote scripts/assets.

Record the exact Cognito email-sending mode, SES identity/region, DKIM status, sandbox/production status, daily/rate quotas, bounce/complaint/suppression handling, relevant DNS record names/status (never secret values), and operational owner. Use observed provider configuration, not documentation-only assumptions.

A real verification message may be tested only with an isolated disposable Cognito account and a non-personal mailbox controlled for acceptance. Enter the OTP interactively; repository/CI evidence may store only redacted outcome, template/config revision, delivery status and timing bucket—never the OTP, recipient address, mailbox content or tokens.
nonFunctionalRequirements: The selected Cognito message type must stay within the current documented subject/body/message-size limits, preserve required placeholders and remain readable in text-only clients. Provider quotas and authentication challenge timing are account/config evidence, not assumed SLOs; verification-code validity follows the provider's verification policy and must be worded from observed/current documentation.
technicalApproach: Use Cognito user-pool message-template configuration with the approved SES sending identity and `DEVELOPER` mode where custom sender/template configuration is selected; do not build a separate email microservice or direct-send OTP path. AWS documents `{####}` for code templates, one EmailMessage body, subject/body limits and configurable From/Reply-To; account/domain verification and SES sandbox status must be checked in the actual selected region. Verification-code validity and authentication challenge duration are separate provider authorities. References: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pool-settings-message-customizations.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/user-pool-email.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/user-pool-settings-email-phone-verification.html, and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito-user-identity-pools/latest/APIReference/API_VerificationMessageTemplateType.html.
apiContract: NOT_APPLICABLE: CS-92 configures provider messages; it adds no application HTTP endpoint. Cognito-managed signup/verification operations remain provider contracts governed by CS-90/CS-91.
persistence: No CareerScope database schema or user-data persistence change. Store only nonsensitive template source and redacted configuration/run evidence. AWS sender secrets, mailbox access and raw messages stay outside Git and test artifacts.
accessibility: Email content must be understandable in text-only clients, use a descriptive subject and readable code/expiry instructions, avoid color-only meaning, and keep the one-time code easy to select/read. Manual assistive-technology review is required for any HTML email styling; no visual acceptance is claimed here.
responsive: Verify the plain-text and HTML message remain readable without horizontal scrolling at narrow mobile widths and at desktop widths; do not embed fixed-width content or remote assets.
browsers: NOT_APPLICABLE to provider configuration itself; real-message content can be inspected in supported desktop/mobile email clients only through a disposable mailbox. Browser QA is not a substitute for actual delivery.
seo: NOT_APPLICABLE: authentication emails and their templates are private and must never be indexed or added to a public sitemap.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: PRIVACY_PII / SECRETS / EXTERNAL_PROVIDER / ABUSE_RATE_LIMITING / DATA_RETENTION. Restrict AWS and DNS changes to explicitly authorized least-privilege operators; never put OTPs, recipient email, raw message, mailbox credentials, access keys, provider tokens or DNS verification secrets in repository evidence. A test message must not be sent to a real candidate or owner account. Preserve Cognito non-enumeration and resend throttles; treat bounce/complaint signals as private operational data with retention/redaction limits.
observability: Record privacy-safe send outcome categories, provider rejection/throttle, bounce/complaint/suppression counts and delivery-latency buckets only where the configured provider provides them. Define the actual alert/owner response path; never log recipient address, OTP, token, full message or mailbox content. If bounce/complaint events are not configured, disclose the gap and keep production acceptance blocked.
manualExternalGates: OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED: exact From/Reply-To, brand/copy approval, supported locale list, expiry wording/duration and support destination. EXTERNAL_GATE: verified SES domain identity and DKIM/DNS status in ap-south-1, Cognito sender configuration, SES sandbox removal/production access and actual quota/bounce/complaint handling. No DNS or AWS changes occur in Phase 3.25; record only redacted evidence.
implementationChecklist: Obtain exact owner From/Reply-To, brand/copy, locale, provider-authoritative verification-code wording and support decisions; do not infer them from the sender-domain target or authentication challenge timing.
Inspect approved Cognito/SES config in the selected region and record sending mode, verified identity/DKIM, sandbox/production and current quotas without secrets.

Create the selected Cognito code-based verification template in the supported EmailMessage shape, with `DEVELOPER` mode and documented subject/body limits, required `{####}` placeholder and provider-authoritative verification wording; omit unnecessary personal data and all credentials/tokens.
Define and test bounce/complaint/suppression handling and the accountable alert/response path using a safe provider test mechanism.

Run static template/placeholder/privacy checks against the single supported EmailMessage shape and verify text-only readability and narrow-screen wrapping without asserting an independently delivered HTML/MIME body.
Send one real message only to an isolated disposable user/mailbox; verify delivery and successful code entry without retaining OTP, address or message contents.
Obtain Product/Security/QA approval and retain redacted configuration/evidence; production sending remains gated on SES access and DNS verification.
risksRecovery: Wrong sender identity or incomplete DNS may cause non-delivery, phishing suspicion or provider rejection. Incorrect provider-authority wording can mislead a user; compare copy to the current selected message-type policy before enabling. If a sender/template change harms delivery, disable Cognito rollout or restore the last approved template/config revision; do not delete identities or rotate unrelated credentials. Bounce/complaint spikes require pausing sends per the approved operator procedure.
definitionOfDone: Implementation DoD: sender/From/Reply-To and locale/copy decisions are approved; Cognito template placeholders and expiry match selected settings; privacy/security checks pass; actual SES identity/DKIM/sandbox/quota/bounce handling are verified; a disposable-account message is delivered and code accepted with no OTP/PII in evidence; Product/Security/QA approve the same revision. Release DoD additionally requires production sender access, domain/DNS proof, current quota/monitoring and production smoke evidence. No AWS, DNS or email was changed during Phase 3.25.

problem: The existing API has an optional Cognito authorization-code start/callback path, but provider OTP signup/resend behavior, verified-email-only owner resolution, privacy-safe failure evidence and disposable-provider acceptance are not established as complete. Current code also accepts a verified phone as an alternate external identity; the approved owner decision makes phone OTP a later capability, so this path must not be treated as current-release approval.
value: Deliver the approved email-first authentication flow without creating a second owner, weakening the existing opaque-session boundary or claiming provider acceptance from local mocks.
functionalRequirements: Current-release scope is email identifier and Cognito-hosted email signup/verification/login. Phone is optional contact only; phone OTP is a later capability under `docs/OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-02.md#CS-90..CS-94` and is excluded here. Do not add a CareerScope OTP or resend endpoint: Cognito-hosted UI owns the OTP entry/resend surface unless a separately approved architecture changes that boundary.

Use the existing `GET /api/auth/cognito/start` and `/api/auth/cognito/callback` contract only while CS-90 approves the exact pool/client/callback configuration. The server starts authorization-code + PKCE using the configured issuer, client and callback, then exchanges the returned code server-to-server and derives identity from verified Cognito profile claims; do not place OTP values, access/refresh tokens or provider secrets in a CareerScope URL, browser storage, logs or repository artifacts.

Create/resolve exactly one CareerScope owner by verified normalized email and provider subject under the approved account-linking rule. A repeated login for the same verified email/subject must resolve the existing owner idempotently, including concurrent same-identity callbacks, without creating a second owner. Missing, unverified, phone-only, ambiguous duplicate-owner or conflicting identity linkage fails closed without creating or transferring ownership. Do not export the existing Argon2 password hash.

After accepted identity, issue only the existing opaque CareerScope application session cookie with the existing `HttpOnly`, `Secure` in HTTPS, `SameSite=Strict`, `/api` scope and expiry semantics. `POST /api/logout` revokes the application session and clears its cookie; do not claim Cognito global sign-out unless separately approved and implemented.

The provider-hosted email OTP resend limit and verification expiry/reuse policy are defined by the approved Cognito pool settings. The application start/callback rate limits remain distinct controls; do not invent provider quotas or describe the current `/api/auth/cognito/start` limiter as OTP resend throttling.

Return only bounded, non-enumerating error categories. Provider outage, invalid/expired/replayed callback state, unverified email, identity collision and disabled Cognito must not issue a session; clear transient state/verifier cookies on callback failure. Keep the current Argon2/session path available while Cognito is disabled or rolled back.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: AUTH_IDENTITY / THIRD_PARTY_INTEGRATION / API_CONTRACT / DATA_MODEL. `apps/api/src/app.ts` composes current `/api/auth/cognito/start`, `/api/auth/cognito/callback`, `/api/session`, `/api/logout` and Argon2 `/api/login`; `packages/core/src/auth.ts` owns application sessions and external identity linking. Preserve these module boundaries; do not add runtime code or schema in this specification phase.
apiContract: EXISTING_CONTRACT: `GET /api/auth/cognito/start` redirects to the configured issuer and sets short-lived HttpOnly state/verifier cookies; `GET /api/auth/cognito/callback` validates the returned code/state, exchanges code server-side, reads provider profile, resolves a verified identity, and redirects with the local opaque session cookie on success; `GET /api/session` reports the application session; `POST /api/logout` revokes the local session. OpenAPI is `apps/api/src/openapi.ts`. `POST /api/register` remains the separate Argon2 route and may be disabled; it is not Cognito OTP signup.

No CareerScope OTP-verification or resend endpoint currently exists or is approved. OTP entry, email verification and resend remain the Cognito-hosted user-pool contract. If an approved provider setup requires an app-owned endpoint, stop for a separately reviewed contract; do not infer one.

Callback must accept only configured redirect URI/issuer and a valid one-time authorization code bound to the short-lived state/verifier; return stable bounded failure categories without echoing provider values. Exact pool/client allowlists and error semantics depend on CS-90 approval and must be marked unresolved until supplied.
persistence: Reuse the current PostgreSQL owner/session/provider-identity persistence implemented by `packages/core/src/auth.ts` and `database.ts`; do not introduce a new OTP table because Cognito owns OTPs. Require unique owner linkage for normalized verified email/provider subject according to the approved migration contract. No owner/profile/application data changes on failed or ambiguous identity; migration/backfill and rollback need separate disposable-Postgres tests before release.
accessibility: CareerScope does not implement the Cognito-hosted OTP controls in this ticket. Hosted-page keyboard, labels, focus/error announcements, contrast, zoom/reflow and manual NVDA/VoiceOver checks remain a provider acceptance gate; the local sign-in link must keep an accessible name and visible focus under its separate UI ticket.
responsive: No new CareerScope layout is introduced. Browser acceptance must confirm the redirect and return path works from mobile, tablet and desktop without a blank/error loop; provider-hosted page reflow is externally validated at 320/390/768/1024/1440 widths when supported.
browsers: Mocked application callback tests target Chromium-independent API integration; browser acceptance for the local entry and provider redirect/return must cover Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Real provider OTP acceptance is a separate external gate, not inferred from the browser suite.
seo: NOT_APPLICABLE: authentication and callback surfaces are private and must remain non-indexable; no identity or callback parameters may enter public metadata or sitemap output.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHENTICATION / AUTHORIZATION / PRIVACY_PII / SECRETS / ABUSE_RATE_LIMITING / AUDIT / DATA_RETENTION. Trust boundaries are browser, CareerScope API/session store, Cognito hosted UI, provider token endpoint and PostgreSQL. Accept verified email and subject only; reject phone-only identity for this scope. Enforce configured redirect allowlists, state/PKCE checks, existing Origin/CSRF behavior for state-changing app routes, session rotation/revocation, account non-enumeration, per-IP/application rate limits and owner-scoped data access. Never log OTP, password, authorization code, state/verifier, tokens, full callback URL, raw provider body or email/phone; redacted category and request correlation only.
observability: Emit privacy-safe counters for start/callback outcome category, throttled requests, provider timeout/unavailability, identity-link conflict and session creation/revocation. Correlate by request ID only; never log OTP, email, phone, callback query, state/verifier, authorization code, access/refresh token or provider response body. Do not claim live dashboards/alerts until measured.
manualExternalGates: HARD DEPENDENCY: CS-90 owner/security approval of user-pool/client/MFA/callback settings and feature-flag/rollback design. EXTERNAL_PROVIDER: disposable Cognito pool/client with approved ap-south-1 configuration, email sender/domain verification, actual hosted email OTP/signup/resend and callback acceptance. No production pool, SMS approval or real owner-account migration is implied; owner account is never used as a test fixture. Historical release metadata remains unchanged; this ticket is optional/email-first and owner-pending for release assignment, not evidence that Cognito is activated.
implementationChecklist: Close CS-90 pool/client/callback/MFA and rollback approval before enabling the route.
Compare current API callback identity handling with the verified-email-only owner decision; reject unverified, phone-only, duplicate and conflicting identities before session creation.
Add deterministic integration coverage for start state/PKCE cookies, valid/invalid callback, provider outage, session issuance/revocation and unchanged Argon2 fallback.
Add privacy assertions over URL, browser storage, application logs and repository/publication artifacts using synthetic sentinels.
Run disposable Cognito email signup/OTP/resend/login/logout and negative cases; capture redacted provider evidence only.
Run cross-owner authorization, Origin/CSRF, cookie and session-revocation tests plus Chromium/Firefox/WebKit auth redirect coverage.
Obtain Security and QA review; document provider-specific manual gates and keep Cognito disabled until exact-SHA canary acceptance.
risksRecovery: Phone-only identity acceptance conflicts with the recorded email-first release boundary and could create or link the wrong owner; fail closed. A provider timeout or partial callback must clear transient cookies and issue no app session. Keep the Argon2 path usable until verified disposable-account E2E, monitoring, owner continuity, backup and rollback gates pass. Never retry a real owner migration from a partially applied state.
definitionOfDone: Implementation DoD: provider-hosted email signup/verification/resend and login work against the approved CS-90 config; verified normalized email resolves one owner; local session cookies/revocation, Origin/CSRF and owner isolation remain intact; phone-only identity is rejected for current release; all negative/privacy/browser tests pass and no OTP/token/PII leaks. Release DoD separately requires disposable Cognito acceptance, protected exact-SHA canary, monitoring, owner continuity and rollback evidence. Phase 3.25 specifies these gates only and performs none of them.

deliveryClassification.rationale: The approved architecture is optional and email-first, with Cognito default-off until owner/security configuration, disposable-provider acceptance and rollback/canary evidence exist. Preserve historical backlog/release metadata; do not infer activation or a product release assignment from the architecture approval.

problem: The source records an identity-authority migration handoff. The 2026-10-02 owner decision already approves important architecture values; do not reopen them or imply Cognito is deployed. Current source still has Argon2id credentials and opaque server-side sessions, and the separate email/provider, frontend and live rollout gates remain distinct tickets.
value: Make the Cognito migration design explicit enough to protect account uniqueness, existing candidate data, browser-session ownership and rollback before any identity cutover.
functionalRequirements: Propagate the owner-approved values from `docs/OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-02.md`: Cognito region `ap-south-1`; normalized/case-insensitive verified email as the primary account identifier; Cognito as hosted identity authority while CareerScope retains its opaque application session after server-side verification/exchange; browser storage never retains Cognito access/refresh tokens; target custom domain `auth.careerscope.tech` after DNS/certificate readiness; existing owner linked once by verified normalized email; existing Argon2 password hashes are never exported; rollout is feature-flagged/canary with the current Argon2/session path available for rollback until disposable-account E2E, monitoring and owner-account continuity pass. These are approved design decisions, not proof of provider configuration or activation.

The same owner-decision record classifies phone number as optional contact initially and phone OTP login as a later capability. Preserve that release boundary unless a newer explicit owner decision is recorded; CS-91's current frozen criteria specify email OTP. Do not infer SMS approval or mobile OTP delivery from email OTP support.

AC1 is partly resolved by the approved region, primary identifier and custom-domain target above. The exact user-pool/client settings, callback/logout allowlists, verification/MFA policy, and operator evidence of actual AWS configuration must be documented without secrets before the design gate can close. The custom domain remains conditional on DNS/certificate readiness.

AC2 flow must specify signup initiation, email OTP verification/resend, login, server callback validation, one-time code/token exchange, CareerScope opaque session issuance/rotation/revocation/logout, recovery behavior from CS-44, rate limits/abuse controls, Cognito outage behavior and rollback to the pre-existing Argon2/session flow. Provider tokens stay server-side and are discarded/redacted after identity verification; do not invent Cognito grants/endpoints beyond official configuration and the existing application contract.

AC3 migration is one-to-one by normalized verified email with a preflight uniqueness/conflict report; create no second owner or duplicate profile, and never transfer local password hashes to Cognito. The user data remains in CareerScope Postgres, linked only after an unambiguous identity match; conflicting/missing/unverified email causes a fail-closed manual resolution, not guessed account merge. Migration execution and backup evidence are separate operational acceptance.

AC4 threat-model review covers browser/provider/API trust boundaries, code/state/nonce/PKCE verification, CSRF/Origin, redirect allowlists, replay, session fixation, account enumeration, OTP abuse, rate limits, email/SMS delivery abuse, provider outage, identity collision, token leakage, retention/deletion and rollback/cutover failure. Security and System Designer must review the same immutable design revision before CS-91 or related implementation may proceed; keep blocked=true metadata until then and preserve the canonical workflow stage.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: AUTH_IDENTITY / THIRD_PARTY_INTEGRATION / API_CONTRACT / DATA_MODEL. Current boundary is `packages/core/src/auth.ts` for Argon2id and server-owned sessions plus the existing PostgreSQL user/profile ownership model. Future Cognito verification is server-to-server; the application issues its existing opaque cookie session and never exposes provider tokens to the browser. Design migration and rollback only; no provider integration, schema, auth route or deployment change is authorized here.
apiContract: No new HTTP endpoint is approved by CS-90. The future design must inventory existing login/session/logout routes and define only the minimal server callback/exchange changes required by an approved Cognito flow, including exact request validation, Origin/CSRF, PKCE/state/nonce, redirect allowlist, generic error/non-enumeration behavior, owner mapping and session rotation. Mark any not-yet-approved callback route as PLANNED, not implemented.
persistence: Preserve existing application user/profile ownership and data. The future identity map must be unique for normalized verified email and external subject, maintain one CareerScope owner, use a reviewed migration/rollback plan, and leave user content in PostgreSQL. Any schema/key/index or retention change requires a separately reviewed migration; do not place OTPs, tokens or passwords in repository state.
accessibility: Architecture-only ticket: no rendered form is implemented here. Future UI tickets must use the approved auth references, accessible OTP labels/errors/status announcements, keyboard/focus/reflow behavior, and manual screen-reader validation.
browsers: NOT_APPLICABLE to this architecture document; future callback/session UI acceptance belongs to CS-91 and the auth-front-end ticket with Chromium, Firefox and WebKit coverage.
seo: NOT_APPLICABLE: authentication and callback routes are private/non-indexable and must not expose identity data in metadata or sitemap output.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHENTICATION / AUTHORIZATION / PRIVACY_PII / SECRETS / ABUSE_RATE_LIMITING / DATA_RETENTION. Trust boundaries are user agent, CareerScope API/session store, Cognito, email/SMS delivery provider and existing Postgres. Verify the provider response server-side; the application remains owner of app sessions and authorization. Allow OAuth authorization code and state only in the required authorization/callback query transport; allow state only in its bounded short-lived HttpOnly transient cookie and the PKCE verifier only in its bounded short-lived HttpOnly transient cookie. Clear both cookies on success and every callback failure, then redirect to a clean application URL. Do not persist these values durably, expose them through logs, analytics, fixtures, Git, evidence or browser storage. OTPs and Cognito access/refresh tokens are never permitted in URLs or browser storage. Never log passwords, verifier/nonce secrets or Cognito tokens; redact callback query values and raw provider errors. Restrict migration scope to the single owner record and preserve data; do not export password hashes or merge on unverified identifiers.
observability: The architecture must name privacy-safe metrics for auth success/failure category, OTP send/verification throttling, provider latency/errors, session exchange/revocation and migration conflicts, with correlation IDs but no email, phone, OTP, token, authorization code, or raw callback URL. Define alerts and a safe rollback signal; live observability remains future evidence.
manualExternalGates: OWNER_DECISION / EXTERNAL_GATE: use approved 2026-10-02 architecture values as the baseline. Phone OTP is already classified as a later capability in that record and is not an unresolved CS-90 decision; CS-91's current frozen criteria specify email OTP. Owner/security review must resolve only the remaining pool/client/MFA/callback configuration; AWS Cognito pool/domain/DNS/SES configuration and live callback/email-OTP acceptance are external and must not be fabricated. SMS approval is a later-release gate, not an email-only acceptance prerequisite. No AWS changes or owner-account migration are performed in Phase 3.25.
implementationChecklist: Reconcile each AC with the 2026-10-02 owner decision and retain exact provenance; do not request region/email/session/domain decisions again.
Inventory current `auth.ts`, session cookies, Origin/CSRF checks, session revocation, user/profile uniqueness and the existing operator recovery path; capture contracts without credentials.

Write one architecture sequence for signup/email verification/login/provider callback/session exchange/logout/recovery/provider outage and rollback, marking Cognito-specific settings as owner/external inputs.
Define normalized-email identity mapping, duplicate/conflict preflight, no-password-hash-export constraint, unchanged user-data ownership and reversible canary/cutover/rollback conditions.

Complete revision-bound Security and System Designer threat-model reviews; keep downstream implementation tickets blocked until owner/external configuration dependencies and design acceptance are explicit.
risksRecovery: A duplicate or ambiguous email mapping can lock out the owner or disclose another account; abort before linking on any mismatch. A failed cutover must keep the current Argon2/session path usable and avoid partial identity changes; rollback must not delete user data, rotate credentials unnecessarily or replay provider tokens.
definitionOfDone: CS-90 specification is complete only when the approved decision provenance is propagated, remaining user-pool/callback/MFA configuration choices are explicitly resolved, migration/rollback and threat model are reviewed by Security and System Designer against the same revision, and no implementation begins before those gates. Provider provisioning, live OTP, account migration and deployment remain separate evidence gates.

problem: Shared atoms and brand/icon states need one source-backed contract; a design reference alone must not be treated as implemented UI or as permission to invent a logo, vector, route or production data.
value: Make the shared primitive boundary deterministic so every later route can reuse accessible stateful controls without visual drift, fabricated content or client-side ownership decisions.
functionalRequirements: Use only the approved upward-growth-arrow identity and canonical token/icon references; if an asset is absent, render an explicit unavailable state rather than inventing SVG or an Engineering mark.

Define button, input, label, status, icon, loader and skeleton contracts for default, focus, disabled, loading and error states; state semantics must remain independent of color and must not expose secrets or PII.

Shared primitives consume real server/API state or explicit empty/unavailable values and do not embed illustrative counts, identities, job records or statuses. RELEASE metadata remains planning evidence, not activation.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: LOCAL_MODULE / CROSS_MODULE. Future implementation belongs to the canonical shared UI/token/icon packages and is consumed by route features; no new API, persistence, owner selector or parallel frontend is introduced.
apiContract: NOT_APPLICABLE: primitives accept typed view state from existing feature/API boundaries; they must not create API clients or infer authorization from visibility.
persistence: NOT_APPLICABLE: no schema, migration, retention or persistence change; browser evidence uses isolated synthetic fixtures only.
accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA: semantic names/labels, keyboard focus, visible focus, disabled/loading semantics, status/error association, reduced motion and manual NVDA/VoiceOver review. Screen-reader evidence remains a human gate.
responsive: Verify 320/390/768/1024/1440 CSS-pixel layouts without unintended horizontal overflow; preserve touch target and text reflow behavior.
browsers: Future component and visual checks cover Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with pinned versions and synthetic state fixtures; missing engine evidence is NOT_RUN.
seo: NOT_APPLICABLE: primitives are internal building blocks; authenticated/private consumers remain noindex.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: INPUT_VALIDATION / PRIVACY_PII. Treat labels, state text and icon names as untrusted display values; do not render tokens, resumes, raw provider data or client-selected owner identifiers. UI state never authorizes an action.
observability: No production telemetry is required for pure primitives. Test evidence records component/state/browser identifiers only, with no user payloads.
visualRegression: Use the named canonical token/icon references and approved desktop/mobile viewport; capture deterministic state variants with minimal masks and an owner-approved threshold. No screenshot may be used as proof of runtime or authorization.
manualExternalGates: UX/Accessibility review of the approved icon identity, state semantics and screen-reader behavior; exact-SHA browser/axe and visual evidence remain future gates.
risksRecovery: A copied or invented asset can create brand inconsistency or expose unsupported product meaning. Revert only the shared primitive change on visual/accessibility regression; no data migration or runtime authorization rollback is implied.
definitionOfDone: Specification DoD: approved asset/token references, state semantics, accessibility/responsive/browser/security boundaries and exact future evidence are explicit; no runtime implementation or fabricated visual pass is claimed.

Future implementation DoD: all listed states render from typed real/unavailable data, axe/keyboard/browser/visual checks pass, manual screen-reader review is recorded and exact release evidence is attached.

implementationChecklistOverride: Inventory canonical tokens, icon map and existing primitives; record missing assets without inventing replacements.
Define typed state contracts and accessible names for each primitive state, including loading, error, unavailable and disabled.
Add component/axe/keyboard tests plus synthetic visual captures at approved desktop/mobile viewports across three engines.
Review redaction and data-source boundaries, then obtain UX, QA, Security and manual accessibility evidence before release activation.

problem: Shared SearchInput, OTPField, FileUpload, Pagination, Toast, ConfirmationDialog, table and component contracts are referenced by approved foundations material but are not yet a ticket-specific implementation-ready boundary.
value: Prevent route-specific form/dialog/table behavior and ensure shared components remain accessible, responsive, source-backed and safe for real API state.
functionalRequirements: Compose only SearchInput, OTPField, FileUpload, Pagination, Toast, ConfirmationDialog and responsive table from CS-105 atoms/tokens; exclude page/shell templates and assign any future template to its owning route ticket.

Define controlled value/change/submit boundaries. OTP paste/edit/validation and resend follow the owning auth contract without inventing code length or provider limits; FileUpload selection/progress/cancellation/error follows the owning resume/storage contract without inventing size/type limits; Pagination emits owning cursor callbacks and never invents totals; ConfirmationDialog resolves only from the owning server result.

FileUpload never exposes raw resume bytes in evidence; Toast and ConfirmationDialog never imply mutation success before the owning server result. The reference is a component contract, not production data or a route.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: LOCAL_MODULE / CROSS_MODULE. Future implementation belongs to canonical shared UI components; API clients, authorization and ownership remain in feature/server boundaries.
apiContract: NOT_APPLICABLE for new endpoints. Components accept typed view models from existing/planned contracts and preserve stable validation/error/concurrency semantics.
persistence: NOT_APPLICABLE: no schema or migration; fixtures are synthetic and isolated.
sharedComponents: Depends on CS-105 atoms/tokens and composes only the seven named components without duplicate route-local primitives or page templates.
accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA: labels, keyboard menu/dialog focus trap/restoration and Escape, upload progress/error association, toast live-region politeness, table headers/overflow, visible focus and reduced motion; NVDA/VoiceOver remains manual.
responsive: Verify 320/390/768/1024/1440 CSS-pixel layouts, deliberate narrow table behavior and touch targets without unintended overflow.
browsers: Future component checks cover Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with pinned versions and synthetic fixtures.
seo: NOT_APPLICABLE: shared authenticated components do not create indexable pages.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: INPUT_VALIDATION / PRIVACY_PII / AUTHORIZATION. Components never authorize actions or trust client owner IDs; upload metadata is untrusted and secrets/tokens/resumes stay out of logs/screenshots.
observability: Record component/state/test identifiers only; no raw input, file bytes, tokens or user data.
visualRegression: Compare the approved component-library reference and UX-approved desktop/mobile matrix with minimal masks and bounded tolerance across three engines; missing evidence is NOT_RUN.
manualExternalGates: UX approval of state/crop/tolerance and manual screen-reader review; exact-SHA browser/axe evidence remains future.
risksRecovery: A generic component can hide authorization or stale-revision failure. Revert the component consumer or flag while preserving server state; no schema rollback is implied.
definitionOfDone: Specification DoD: named components, interaction/server-state boundaries, failure/accessibility/responsive/security/visual gates and no-fabrication rules are explicit. Future implementation DoD requires component/browser/axe/manual evidence and owning-contract tests.

problem: The cross-surface accessibility, responsive and locale contract is broad and does not yet state which observable states, actors, viewports and authorization boundaries must be verified without claiming unsupported translations or product capabilities.
value: Give each current route a repeatable accessibility and reflow evidence boundary while preserving server ownership, honest unavailable states and the existing release gates.
functionalRequirements: The current implemented route census for this specification is exactly `/`, `/dashboard`, `/jobs`, `/applications`, `/saved`, `/resume`, `/career-resources`, `/settings` and `/preparation`; derive the list from the tracked Next.js page source and record the route-to-state manifest. Marketing, admin and other design-referenced future routes are future applicability only, inherit this contract when implemented, and do not block present-state specification approval or count as implemented routes.

For every applicable current route, enumerate the rendered keyboard path, focus order, visible focus, labels, errors/status announcements, dialog Escape/focus restoration and reduced-motion behavior; use the route's real or explicit unavailable state rather than adding a route or capability.

Exercise 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 CSS-pixel viewports with long text and narrow tables; assert no ordinary-content horizontal overflow, deliberate table behavior and usable touch targets. Locale-aware number/date formatting must use the owning formatter and must not claim translations that are not present.

The current route-state accessibility matrix must include keyboard-only traversal, skip-navigation where a landmark shell exposes it, labelled forms, error/status announcements, dialog focus entry, Escape handling, focus restoration and reduced-motion behavior for each applicable route/state. A missing screen-reader run remains HUMAN_VALIDATION_REQUIRED, not an automated pass.

Responsive assertions must record document and intentional-scroll-container widths at every required viewport, identify any table/list container that may scroll intentionally, assert long text wrapping without layout breakage, usable controls, visible focus and reachable responsive navigation; reduced-motion must preserve operation and announcements.

Locale verification must inject an explicit supported locale/timezone into the application's existing formatter seam where one exists and compute the expected date/number/currency output through the standards-based Intl contract. If no injection seam exists, record the smallest future test seam required; do not use ambient OS locale or add a translation catalogue.

Run positive, denied, malformed, expired-session, stale-revision and dependency-failure fixtures through the existing session-derived ownership/API contracts; UI visibility never grants a role or capability and no private payload is captured in evidence.

The security fixture matrix must contain a synthetic positive owner, anonymous request, expired session, cross-owner resource, malformed input, stale revision for revisioned mutations and dependency-failure case where the route uses a dependency. Each expected denial is asserted at the server/API boundary with the documented status/error and no protected read/write side effect.

Keep RELEASE metadata as a fail-closed acceptance state. Activation requires the declared automated, browser, manual screen-reader and authorization evidence; this ticket does not implement product routes, auth, localization catalogues or provider integrations.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: CROSS_MODULE / API_CONTRACT. The future checks consume canonical route components and the same-origin API client; they do not create a second frontend, client-side authorization, persistence or a parallel locale system.

The actor is an authenticated candidate or an anonymous visitor encountering a safe session-expired/unavailable state. The route census is a test/specification boundary only: it does not create routes, alter Next.js composition or change server authorization. Current route owners remain the existing page modules and Fastify contracts; future marketing/admin routes inherit this contract only after their own route/design/API specifications exist.
apiContract: NOT_APPLICABLE for new endpoints. Existing routes and session-derived ownership remain authoritative; assertions must use registered contracts and stable error semantics.

The shared `GET /api/session` contract returns HTTP 200 with `{authenticated:false,registrationEnabled,cognitoEnabled}` anonymously or `{authenticated:true,csrf,email,phone,owner,aiEnabled}` for a valid local session; only the 64-character owner digest is exposed, never the raw owner/session/provider token. Applicable route fixtures must use the registered method/status/error contract and must not invent endpoints for future surfaces.
persistence: NOT_APPLICABLE: no schema or migration. Locale/display fixtures are synthetic and must not persist user data.
accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA: semantic landmarks/headings, accessible names and labels, keyboard traversal, visible focus, dialog focus trap/restoration and Escape, status/error association and announcements, non-color state indication, reduced motion and manual NVDA/VoiceOver review.
responsive: Verify 320/390/768/1024/1440 CSS-pixel layouts, long-content reflow, intentional narrow table handling and touch targets without unintended horizontal scrolling.
browsers: Future automated checks cover Chromium, Firefox and WebKit at the approved viewport matrix; missing engine or manual evidence is NOT_RUN, not a pass.
seo: NOT_APPLICABLE to authenticated/internal cross-surface checks; private surfaces remain noindex and must not place user data in metadata.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHORIZATION / PRIVACY_PII / INPUT_VALIDATION. Session identity and server policy determine access; never infer capability from rendered controls, never trust client-selected owner IDs, and keep tokens, resumes, OTPs and private payloads out of screenshots, fixtures, logs and reports.

Trust boundary: browser route, query/body values, rendered controls, locale/timezone inputs and test fixture data are untrusted; the authenticated server session is the principal source and the owning API/repository is the resource authority. Positive owner O1 may read/write only O1 resources; anonymous and expired sessions receive the registered unauthenticated contract; O2 cannot read or mutate O1; malformed/stale/dependency failures return their documented safe errors with no protected read/write. Rate limits, CSRF/origin checks, redaction and audit/correlation requirements remain those of each existing route.
observability: Record only route/state/viewport/browser/build identifiers and failure categories; redact request bodies and personal data. Evidence must preserve correlation without leaking user content.
visualRegression: Use approved reference paths and exact viewport/browser manifests where a visual comparison is applicable; masks must be minimal and must not cover controls, focus, errors or substantive content. The current visual/accessibility matrix contains only `/`, `/dashboard`, `/jobs`, `/applications`, `/saved`, `/resume`, `/career-resources`, `/settings` and `/preparation`; marketing/admin/future design references are listed separately as DESIGN_NOT_CURRENT/PLANNED_DESIGN_ONLY and are not represented as implemented surfaces or current pass criteria.
manualExternalGates: Manual NVDA/VoiceOver observation, UX acceptance of responsive/locale states and exact-SHA browser/axe evidence remain future gates; no hosted or live result is claimed in Phase 3.25.
risksRecovery: A global accessibility or formatting assertion can hide a route-specific authorization or stale-state defect. Scope failures to the route/state fixture and revert only the test/contract change; preserve server data and do not weaken the gate.
definitionOfDone: Specification DoD: route/state matrix, exact accessibility/reflow/locale assertions, ownership/security boundaries, negative cases and future evidence owners are explicit; no runtime capability or translation is fabricated.
Future implementation DoD: applicable component/browser/axe checks, responsive matrix, manual screen-reader evidence and route-owner contract tests pass on the reviewed SHA before activation.

implementationChecklistOverride: Inventory current routes and state contracts from the design index and route/API sources; exclude absent routes and unsupported translations.
Define the route-by-viewport accessibility, focus, announcement, reduced-motion and narrow-content assertion matrix with synthetic/redacted fixtures.
