problem: The repository has a shared route/permission and transactional UX contract, but no single ticket-specific matrix currently proves how route surface, authenticated principal, server permission, release state, feature flag, denial behavior and high-risk mutation confirmation compose. UI visibility must not become authorization, and planned contracts must not be mistaken for implemented endpoints.
value: Give implementation and reviewers one fail-closed contract for authorization boundaries and transactional interactions, reducing privilege-escalation, duplicate-command, stale-revision and unsafe-release risk without broadening any product surface.
functionalRequirements: Maintain a machine-readable route/role/release/flag matrix from authoritative route registrations and approved design contracts. Every entry names surface, authentication requirement, server permission, release/feature gate and safe unauthorized/unavailable behavior; an omitted route remains absent rather than implicitly public.

Server/API authorization derives the principal and resource owner from the authenticated session and persisted data. Client-selected owner IDs, roles, permissions, flags, consent, route visibility and browser storage never grant access; direct unauthorized requests are denied before protected reads or writes.

For high-risk mutations, the owning domain contract must require explicit confirmation and, where specified, reason capture, idempotency/replay protection, revision or lease/fencing checks, and an immutable safe audit event. CS-104 does not invent a mutation endpoint or generic admin database operation.

Positive, unauthenticated, unauthorized, malformed, stale/conflicting, duplicate, unavailable and provider/queue failure fixtures map to each existing or explicitly planned contract. UI pending/disabled/denied state is a presentation of server result, never a security control.

Release or feature metadata alone cannot activate a surface. Activation requires the declared route, permission, domain contract, security/privacy, accessibility, hosted/release and rollback evidence; current ticket state remains BACKLOG/RELEASE and no runtime activation occurs in Phase 3.25.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: CROSS_MODULE / API_CONTRACT / ASYNC_SYSTEM. Keep route composition in the canonical Next.js/Fastify modules and use existing session, CSRF/origin, idempotency, revision, outbox, lease and fencing abstractions where their domain contracts already exist. This ticket defines the contract and matrix; it does not add a new service, route, database model or queue.

SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHENTICATION, AUTHORIZATION, ADMIN_PRIVILEGE, INPUT_VALIDATION, ABUSE_RATE_LIMITING and AUDIT. Treat the browser as untrusted and enforce all boundaries on the server before repository access; fail closed when a permission, release, revision or capability result is missing, stale or unavailable.
apiContract: Use EXISTING_CONTRACT entries only where they are present in apps/api/src/app.ts and the documented API surface. For a future child capability, specify PLANNED_CONTRACT separately with method, route, actor, auth, authorization, request validation, response allowlist, stable errors and ownership before registration; do not invent paths in CS-104.

Every mutating contract preserves canonical CSRF/origin protections, stable 400/401/403/404/409/429/5xx semantics as applicable, idempotency or revision behavior where required, and no protected read on denial. UI route visibility and feature metadata are not authorization evidence.
persistence: NOT_APPLICABLE for new persistence in CS-104. Existing owner-scoped entities, revisions, outbox commands, leases and audit records remain authoritative. Any child migration must define constraints, uniqueness, retention, rollback and recovery in its own ticket before implementation.
accessibility: Contract-driven pending, disabled, denied, expired, conflict and failure states must have semantic status/error associations, keyboard-operable confirmation controls, visible focus, focus restoration after dialogs, and non-color-only explanation. Automated axe/browser evidence and a separate NVDA/VoiceOver judgment remain future gates; inaccessible UI cannot be excused by a server denial.
responsive: Shared confirmation/error/pending patterns must remain usable at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 CSS pixels with no unintended overflow, clipped focus or inaccessible touch targets. This shared contract does not create a new visual page; feature-specific layouts remain owned by their tickets.
browsers: Future component/browser verification covers Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with synthetic principals and contract fixtures. Missing browser or contract evidence is NOT_RUN, never PASS.
seo: NOT_APPLICABLE for this internal contract; authenticated/private surfaces remain noindex and no route matrix entry may expose permission, operational or user data through metadata.
securityPrivacy: Trust boundary: client route, method, IDs, headers, roles, flags, revisions, reason text and consent claims are untrusted. The session establishes the principal; repository queries enforce ownership and least privilege. Admin privilege is an allowlisted domain capability, not generic database access.

Sensitive fields include sessions, CSRF values, provider tokens, resumes, contact data, audit details and infrastructure metadata. Redact them from logs, error bodies, fixtures, screenshots and telemetry. Rate-limit authentication and high-risk mutations according to existing contracts; audit actor, action, target, reason, correlation ID and safe result without secrets or raw PII.

Abuse cases include direct-route privilege escalation, owner-ID substitution, stale-session replay, duplicate mutation, stale revision overwrite, forged confirmation/reason, malformed input, provider timeout and queue/DLQ failure. Each owning contract must return a safe error and preserve data/event invariants.
observability: Use existing request/correlation IDs and safe outcome categories for allow, deny, conflict, duplicate, retry, timeout and unavailable states. Record audit events only for approved mutations; never log credentials, tokens, raw resumes, request bodies or fabricated success metrics.
visualRegression: DESIGN_NOT_APPLICABLE for the shared contract itself. Feature tickets that render confirmation, denial or transactional states must bind their own approved screen/state reference and visual evidence; no screenshot is treated as an authorization or data contract.
manualExternalGates: Security and release reviewers must approve the route/role/release/flag matrix and high-risk mutation contract before activation. Hosted exact-SHA CI, live authorization/rollback evidence and human accessibility review remain future gates where required; no operator or production action is performed by this specification.
risksRecovery: Primary risks are UI-only authorization, overbroad admin capability, duplicate or stale mutation, and partial async effects. On a denied/unknown/stale result, perform no protected read/write and render the contract-defined safe state. On a conflict, preserve the current revision and require refresh/review; on an outbox/worker failure, retain at-least-once/idempotent/fenced semantics. Rollback removes the contract consumer or flag, not historical audit/data.
definitionOfDone: Specification DoD: route matrix fields and denial semantics are explicit; existing versus planned contracts are distinguished; ownership, CSRF/origin, idempotency/revision/fencing, audit/redaction, failure states, accessibility/responsive/browser gates and release boundary are ticket-specific; no runtime/API/schema implementation is claimed.

Future implementation DoD: every matrix entry has server tests for positive/denial/malformed/failure paths; high-risk mutations have confirmation/reason/idempotency/concurrency/audit evidence; UI states are keyboard/axe/browser verified; hosted exact-SHA, security, rollback and human accessibility evidence are recorded before RELEASE activation.

implementationChecklistOverride: Inventory current route registrations, session/CSRF/origin checks, API schemas, ownership queries, revision/idempotency/lease abstractions and documented feature flags; record absent contracts without inventing replacements.
Build the route/role/release/flag matrix with explicit server permission and safe denial/unavailable behavior; link each entry to its owning ticket and source contract.
For each existing or planned high-risk mutation, document confirmation, reason, idempotency, concurrency/fencing, audit and rollback requirements without adding endpoints here.
Add synthetic unit/contract/security fixtures for allow, denial-before-read, malformed, duplicate, stale/conflict, timeout and unavailable paths; add browser/accessibility checks for shared states.
Review redaction, rate limits, ownership and admin least privilege with Security; obtain exact-SHA hosted/release and manual accessibility evidence before activation.

problem: The approved production-operations board groups privileged operational areas, but the repository has no active CS-103 operations shell, route, operations-data API, admin principal contract or telemetry-backed view contract. Design labels and illustrated values cannot establish that any host, provider, queue, database, backup, security event or deployment state exists.
value: Provide a bounded future navigation/frame for approved production-operations screens while keeping private operational data, candidate PII and privileged mutations inaccessible until each has an explicit server-side contract and authorization gate.
functionalRequirements: CS-103 owns only the FUTURE production-operations workspace frame/navigation boundary in the separate Admin Control Plane. It does not create a standalone route or own the operational pages; child ownership follows design/DESIGN-INDEX.json#admin-production-operations (CS-201–CS-212, CS-24, CS-25, CS-26, CS-27, CS-30 and CS-86) and cross-cutting design/accessibility ownership follows CS-105–CS-108.

The proposed `stage_11_enabled` registry value is planning metadata only. With current FUTURE/default-false configuration, no production-operations entry, direct route, API, telemetry request or mutation becomes active because this ticket or a design asset exists.

In a separately authorized future shell, navigation and rendered states are derived from server-authoritative authenticated administrative access and permitted capability data. Missing, unknown, expired, revoked or failed authorization must render the approved safe denial/unavailable state and issue no operations-data read; hiding a control is never authorization.

The shell itself performs no mutation, replay, retry, deploy, restore, flag change, user lookup, consent change, provider configuration, database query or generic administrative action. Every such operation remains owned by its child contract and must be authorized and audited server-side.

Use real contract-backed health/telemetry only when supplied by the owning child API. Unknown, delayed, empty, stale or unavailable telemetry is labeled as such; never render design-board names, counts, costs, percentages, timestamps, host states, queue states, logs or security events as production data.

Render no secret, token, cookie, authorization header, raw resume, raw candidate record or unnecessary PII in navigation, shell chrome, metadata, logs, telemetry, browser storage or screenshots. Operational messages are redacted by the server contract before the shell receives them.

This ticket does not define or expose a generic database console, unrestricted raw log viewer, secret reveal, credential rotation UI, candidate-wide data browser, security/compliance certification, or any child operational workflow. A design label or admin privilege does not authorize these capabilities.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: CROSS_MODULE presentation boundary in the existing Next.js application and shared UI, nested within the future Admin Control Plane. SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHENTICATION, AUTHORIZATION, PRIVACY_PII, SECRETS, ADMIN_PRIVILEGE and AUDIT. No API, identity provider, database entity, telemetry collector, queue, worker, route or deployment control is created by this shell ticket.

Reuse the canonical authenticated layout and shared primitives after CS-95. Keep operation-specific read/write behavior in child tickets and server modules; treat the UI as a consumer of allowlisted, redacted view models rather than a security boundary. Route/role/release/flag decisions must use the approved CS-104 contract before any future shell activation.
apiContract: NOT_APPLICABLE for CS-103 itself: the shell adds no endpoint, request, response, polling stream or mutation. Child APIs must declare actor, server authorization, field allowlist/redaction, error semantics, retention, audit and observability independently; no route or response shape is inferred from screenshots.
persistence: NOT_APPLICABLE: the shell persists no admin identity, permissions, operational events, metrics, logs, secrets, candidate records or UI-derived authorization. Do not cache privileged view models or authorization decisions in local/session storage. Retention and audit storage belong to the independently specified child data contracts.
accessibility: Future shell navigation must use named semantic landmarks and links, programmatic current-page state, visible focus, logical keyboard order, text labels for disabled/unavailable entries, keyboard/touch operation for mobile disclosure, and non-color-only status. Permission/session pending, denied, expired and load-error states must be announced without disclosing protected operational details. Human NVDA or VoiceOver testing remains a separate required acceptance gate; axe is not a human screen-reader result.
responsive: Use the canonical production-operations board only as frame context; panel 14 illustrates selected mobile pages, not a separately approved CS-103 shell crop. Before visual implementation acceptance, UX must identify the shell/navigation subset and approve its mobile navigation state. Verify 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 CSS-pixel widths, focus/touch usability and no unintended horizontal overflow; do not scale the desktop board or expose child screen content in the parent.
browsers: Future acceptance covers Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with exact browser versions and authorized shell states. Missing engines or missing authorization fixtures are NOT_RUN, not PASS. Use synthetic admin principals and sanitized telemetry fixtures only.
seo: NOT_APPLICABLE: the Admin Control Plane is authenticated and private. Any future operations routes must be noindex and must not expose operational state, user data, secrets or internal host metadata through metadata, canonical URLs, previews or sitemaps.
securityPrivacy: Trust boundary: browser and all client-selected IDs, roles, permissions, flags and consent claims are untrusted; the session and API derive the principal and every capability. Resource owners vary by child domain; candidate data remains candidate-owned, and admin access is least-privilege operational access, not ownership transfer.

The shell receives only a server-authorized navigation/view model and has no direct database, host, provider or secret-manager access. Reject or safely deny unauthenticated, unauthorized, expired/revoked session, stale capability, malformed state and failed permission resolution before any child data read. Never use a UI flag or route visibility as authorization.

Operational logs/telemetry may contain security-sensitive infrastructure details and PII. Require child APIs to redact passwords, secrets, access/refresh tokens, cookies, authorization headers, resume contents, full email/phone, raw request bodies and unnecessary identifiers before returning or logging data. Do not expose raw credentials, arbitrary shell/database controls, or unbounded cross-candidate reads.

Potential abuse includes privilege escalation by direct URL/API call, cross-role access, stale-session replay, query/filter injection, log/metric cardinality abuse, secret enumeration and use of the shell to trigger destructive operations. The shell defines no mutation/query endpoint; child tickets must specify rate limits, audit events, reason capture and confirmation where their operation risk requires them.
observability: The shell adds no operational telemetry or audit record. Future child APIs expose only contract-defined safe status categories and request correlation IDs; they must distinguish success, empty, stale, denied, unavailable and error without logging response payloads or secrets. Never substitute generated metrics for missing telemetry.
visualRegression: DESIGN_PARTIAL / NON_BLOCKING for specification: the design index assigns a full 16-panel production-operations board to CS-103 and identifies selected mobile examples, but does not map a dedicated shell-only crop, exact shell state or mobile navigation frame. This is sufficient to specify a FUTURE reusable shell boundary, not sufficient to claim exact shell parity. UX must select the crop/state, approve mobile behavior, dynamic masks and numeric tolerance before visual implementation acceptance; no illustrated operational values may be used as fixtures or expected production values.
manualExternalGates: MANUAL_PRODUCT / UX: approve the production-operations shell-only crop, mobile navigation, and predeclared visual comparison tolerance before implementation acceptance. SECURITY / RELEASE GATE: CS-104 must establish route, admin role, release/feature-flag and safe-denial semantics; each child operational ticket must establish its API, data allowlist, authorization, audit and retention contract before the shell exposes it. MANUAL_ACCESSIBILITY: a qualified human completes the NVDA or VoiceOver smoke test on the authorized future build. No operator/host action is performed by this specification.
risksRecovery: Primary risks are treating the admin shell as authorization, rendering invented/overbroad telemetry, or leaking secrets/PII through logs and shell metadata. Default to no route/data and fail closed on missing/stale permission. On a future permission-loss or fetch error, discard sensitive view state and return to the contract-defined denial/unavailable screen. Rollback removes shell presentation only; it must not alter host, queue, backup, provider or candidate data.
definitionOfDone: Specification DoD: shell-only FUTURE scope; child and cross-cutting ownership; canonical board and partial-design/non-blocking rationale; no invented route/API/schema; server-side permission, redaction and no-fake-telemetry rules; pending/empty/error/denial/expiry behavior; accessibility/responsive/browser requirements; all exact AC bindings; no runtime implementation claim.

Future implementation/release DoD: CS-104 route/role/release contract and each exposed child API/data/security contract are approved; default hidden remains enforced; direct unauthorized requests cause zero protected reads; only redacted contract-backed state renders; all actions are owned and audited by child APIs; desktop/mobile visual and browser/a11y checks pass; human screen-reader validation and exact-SHA release gate evidence are recorded.

implementationChecklistOverride: Inventory current admin route, session/permission boundary and operations data/API sources; record absence without reading production data or logs.
Confirm CS-104 route/role/flag denial contract and map the parent shell to the admin production-operations board while preserving child IDs and screen ownership.
Define only the shared frame/navigation view model; identify each destination by approved child ownership and server-derived permission.
Keep shell unavailable by default; connect only allowlisted redacted server state after the owning child API and audit contract exists.
Add synthetic authorization, redaction, pending/empty/error/expired and zero-read denial tests; add keyboard/axe and visual/responsive acceptance.
Complete human NVDA/VoiceOver review, exact-SHA release evidence and documentation before any separately authorized activation.

problem: The approved recruiter board describes a FUTURE workspace, but the current repository does not provide a recruiter product route, recruiter authorization/session contract, candidate-consent persistence contract, or recruiter API. The ticket is a reusable shell boundary; it must not treat board data or proposed `stage_9_enabled` metadata as proof that recruiter functionality is active.
value: Keep a future recruiter experience visually and architecturally composable while preventing shell/navigation visibility from becoming authorization or disclosing candidate data before server-enforced recruiter permissions and current candidate consent exist.
functionalRequirements: CS-102 owns only a reusable recruiter workspace frame/navigation boundary. It does not assign a standalone URL; child screens remain owned by CS-177–CS-192, and their routes/actions are not inferred from image labels.

The recruiter surface remains FUTURE and hidden/unavailable under the current product configuration. The registry's proposed `stage_9_enabled` value is planning metadata, not an existing runtime feature flag or authorization decision.

In any separately authorized future rendering, the shell receives only a server-derived recruiter principal, permission result, and candidate-visibility result from approved contracts. If recruiter authentication, candidate consent, permission, or scope is absent, unknown, expired, or withdrawn, render no candidate-specific content and do not cache it; use the finalized safe denial/unavailable behavior from the route-permission contract.

Never accept a recruiter identity, candidate owner ID, consent state, role, or permission from a client-selected value as authority. Navigation hiding is not access control; each child API must enforce authorization independently.

The shell does not implement candidate search, match scoring, profile/resume/contact access, job posting, outreach, messaging, pipeline mutation, interview scheduling, analytics, company management or settings. These are separate child tickets and contracts.

All board names, counts, match values, candidate identities, messages, company values and statuses are illustrative. Use only contract-backed data or an explicit empty/unavailable state; unknown remains unknown.

No shell action may imply candidate consent, recruiter privilege, successful outreach, interview state, application state, or verified candidate data. Do not rank on protected traits, scrape unauthorized sources, expose secrets, or send messages from shell navigation.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: CROSS_MODULE presentation boundary over the canonical Next.js authenticated layout, shared UI primitives and future recruiter child features; no route, API, provider, database entity, queue or worker is created by this ticket.

Use the existing recruiter full reference board as contextual visual authority for the shared frame only. Keep individual screen geometry and business operations with CS-177–CS-192. Route/role/release/feature-flag and server denial behavior must follow CS-104's route-permission contract before implementation; shared UI primitives follow CS-95/CS-106 where applicable.
apiContract: NOT_APPLICABLE for CS-102 itself: it defines no HTTP endpoint, request or persistence operation. Any recruiter read or mutation must be separately specified by its owning child ticket and server contract; this shell specification does not invent route paths, data shapes, consent endpoints, status codes, or candidate fields.
persistence: NOT_APPLICABLE: the shell stores no recruiter identity, candidate record, consent, profile, resume, contact detail, message, campaign, pipeline state or audit event. Do not persist UI-derived permissions or consent state in browser storage. Data/consent persistence and retention require an independently approved domain contract before any child implementation.
securityPrivacy: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: CROSS_MODULE. SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHENTICATION, AUTHORIZATION, PRIVACY_PII, ADMIN_PRIVILEGE boundary separation, AUDIT for future sensitive child actions, and DATA_RETENTION for any future candidate disclosure.

Trust boundary: browser is untrusted; API/session and consent/permission service are authoritative. Candidate remains the data owner. Recruiter reads are limited to the exact fields and purpose authorized by a current server-validated consent and role policy; shell must fail closed on missing or stale decisions. No raw resume or contact information is allowed in shell chrome, navigation metadata, logs, screenshots or telemetry.

The shell must not provide an admin/database control surface or reuse candidate permissions as recruiter permissions. Any future privileged action is a child contract, must be least-privilege, server-authorized and auditable, and must not accept client-provided owner identity.
accessibility: The shared frame must preserve semantic navigation/landmarks, a programmatic current-page state, visible keyboard focus, logical tab order, accessible names for navigation controls, Escape/focus restoration for any separately approved dialog, and non-color-only active/disabled indicators. problem: CS-101 is a cross-cutting truthfulness and capability-gating boundary, not the owner of the AI Apply Assistant screen. value: Prevent the candidate UI from promising, exposing or invoking AI behavior that is not implemented, authorized and enabled, while preserving the existing deterministic preparation report and user-controlled decisions.
functionalRequirements: For the current capability, the authenticated `/preparation` surface may render the per-item `Get AI coaching` control only when the server-derived session reports `aiEnabled: true`; pending, unauthenticated, expired or false capability state renders no active AI control. When the candidate explicitly activates one preparation item, display only the server response for that item with the visible `AI-generated coaching` label. Render response text as escaped text, never HTML. A 503 capability-disabled response renders the explicit unavailable message; other failures remain errors and never substitute a sample answer.

No AI application assistant route, application submission, resume rewrite, cover-letter generation, arbitrary chat, scoring, ranking, eligibility, matching exclusion, ownership or application-lifecycle action is introduced by CS-101. The candidate remains the sole authority for submitting an application and opening an external destination never marks Applied.

The AI Apply Assistant reference screen remains owned by CS-130. CS-101 may specify the shared capability/truthfulness boundary only; it does not transfer screen ownership, invent a route, assign admin access or treat design-board sample values as product data. Admin model/billing/flag surfaces remain separate tickets and are not exposed by this candidate boundary.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: CROSS_MODULE presentation boundary over the existing Next.js session and preparation feature; no new API, route, provider, database entity or worker. persistence: NOT_APPLICABLE: CS-101 creates no AI/application record and persists no prompt, completion, resume content, provider token or client-side capability state. Existing preparation state and API ownership semantics remain unchanged.
accessibility: For the existing preparation control, the enabled button must have the visible/accessibly named action, be keyboard activatable, expose pending state without duplicate requests, and announce a returned error through the existing alert semantics. observability: Use existing request correlation and safe outcome categories only. Never log prompt/response text, resume/profile data, cookies, CSRF values, OpenRouter credentials or raw provider bodies. No new metric, dashboard or successful live provider claim is implied by this specification.

engineeringEpics.title: Engineering delivery and repository state integrity
Deterministic discovery, matching and owner-scoped data

productInvariants: Candidate owns profile, resume, saved jobs and application decisions. Opening an external application destination never marks Applied.
Do not fabricate ATS/interview/offer/rejection events, unknown data, analytics or verification claims.
Matching remains deterministic; AI cannot silently replace scores, ranking or exclusions.
No autonomous auto-apply, credential/cookie/session theft, CAPTCHA bypass or provider terms/rate-limit bypass.
HOLD/FUTURE features and unapproved provider capabilities stay disabled; design approval is not activation authority.
No new service, technology, schema or endpoint is prescribed merely to reproduce a screenshot.
security: Actor and ownership: authenticated session derives owner; client IDs never choose ownership. Test foreign-owner denial without object-existence disclosure.
Mutations require authoritative validation, same-origin CSRF protection and domain-specific concurrency/idempotency constraints.
Candidate profile/resume/application notes are private; keep raw data, cookies, OAuth/provider tokens, secrets and configuration out of logs, exports, screenshots and evidence.
Admin/recruiter roles require explicit RBAC and consent-scoped projections. No generic database console or unrestricted raw-resume endpoint.
Retention, erasure and audit details must follow the approved domain contract; no undocumented new retention period.
Exercise malformed input, unauthorized actor, stale revision, disabled capability, duplicate request and provider failure where the feature touches those boundaries.
definitionOfDone: Each acceptance criterion has named executable assertions or a dated manual procedure and expected result.
Required unit/integration/contract/browser/accessibility/privacy checks pass for current content under Node >=24; no skips/retries conceal failure.
Documentation and contract agree with implementation; historical evidence is not presented as a new run.
Independent current-content review resolves specification/implementation findings before promotion.
Manual/provider/live gates remain explicit and unexecuted until observed; PROD requires exact reviewed deployed revision acceptance.
Rollback/recovery plan preserves data and encryption material; no irreversible shipping action is authorized by completing a specification.

accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA target: semantic headings/landmarks, accessible names, labels/instructions and associated validation errors. The required manual NVDA/VoiceOver review must identify browser, assistive-technology version, build/revision, and the ticket's actual supported state inventory, with observed announcement/focus order and exact failure condition. Auth-specific states such as invalid/expired, success and signed-out are required only when the ticket contract supports them; otherwise record them as NOT_APPLICABLE with the contract citation. Automated axe output is not a substitute.
Keyboard-only navigation with visible focus, logical order, Escape/focus trap/restoration for dialogs, and status/error announcements for async operations.
Non-color status indicators, contrast review, reduced motion and zoom/reflow; NVDA/VoiceOver judgment remains future HUMAN VALIDATION.
responsive: Verify 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440px; ordinary content does not cause horizontal overflow; tables have deliberate narrow-screen behavior.
Use mapped approved reference geometry; touch targets and long localized text remain usable; do not invent unsupported mobile designs.
publicSeo: For public/indexable pages: truthful semantic title/description, canonical URL, robots, Open Graph, sitemap and valid structured data where supported.
No private data, fake user counts, fabricated customer claims or future features advertised as active.

approach: Use the canonical root workspace and existing modules; inspect callers and tests before changing a contract.
nonFunctional: Preserve bounded input, deterministic behavior, cancellation/retry semantics and current performance regression thresholds where applicable; do not claim a production SLO.
default.persistence: Preserve owner-scoped PostgreSQL constraints, revisions and append-only migrations; no new database change is inferred from this spec.
default.api: Use registered Fastify routes and the single same-origin client; new operations need reviewed schemas and negative authorization contracts.
observability: Correlate safe request/command/execution identifiers; record failure categories and health without sensitive payloads.

default.recovery: Restore the prior reviewed code/configuration; preserve stored data and validate migrations separately. Host execution is a later authorized step.

CS-108-AC2.preconditions: Synthetic owner, foreign-owner, unauthenticated, malformed and dependency-failure fixtures map to existing server contracts.
CS-108-AC2.setup: Join each applicable matrix row to the registered route/API contract in docs/API-SURFACE.md and its server route source; for rows without a contract use a required NOT_APPLICABLE/unavailable fixture. Run positive and denial cases through the existing same-origin client/server boundary with redacted fixture data and no production writes.
CS-108-AC2.procedure: Use a frozen expected-contract table checked into the matrix, not the implementation under test. Scope AC2 to operations actually referenced by the nine current page routes (profile, saved/leads, resume, jobs/search, preparation and settings), plus the shared GET /api/session owner/auth boundary; authentication start/callback/logout, scheduled discovery, market/pipeline, admin and other provider/control-plane routes are explicitly out of this visual-acceptance criterion and remain owned by their dedicated tickets. GET /api/session must return HTTP 200 with `{authenticated:false,registrationEnabled:boolean,cognitoEnabled:boolean}` anonymously, or HTTP 200 with `{authenticated:true,csrf,email,phone,owner,aiEnabled}` for a valid local session; owner is exactly a 64-character SHA-256 digest and raw session tokens, provider tokens and raw owner IDs must never appear. GET /api/profile returns HTTP 200 with the owner profile or the documented revision-zero empty record, HTTP 401 when unauthenticated and HTTP 429 after the owner-keyed read budget; PUT /api/profile returns HTTP 200 on a valid owner save, 400 for malformed input, 401 unauthenticated, 403 Origin/CSRF failure, 409 for a stale revision with no row/event change, and 429 after the owner-keyed update budget. GET /api/leads returns HTTP 200 owner rows, 401 unauthenticated and 429 after the owner-keyed read budget; GET /api/leads/:id and /history return HTTP 200 for an owned record, safe HTTP 404 for missing or foreign records, 400 for malformed IDs, 401 unauthenticated and 429 for the read budget; GET /api/leads/by-job/:jobId returns HTTP 200 with `{lead:null}` for an unknown job, HTTP 400 for a malformed UUID, HTTP 401 unauthenticated and HTTP 429 for the read budget, and never returns another owner's lead. POST /api/leads returns HTTP 200 for a valid owner save, 400 for malformed input, 401 unauthenticated, 403 Origin/CSRF failure, 404 when the completed job is absent, and 429 after the owner-keyed update budget; PUT /api/leads/:id returns HTTP 200 for a valid update, 400 malformed input, 401 unauthenticated, 403 Origin/CSRF failure, 404 for missing or foreign leads, 409 for a stale revision where supported, and 429 after the owner-keyed update budget. The frozen table also lists: POST /api/searches (202 success; 400 malformed; 401 unauthenticated; 403 CSRF; 409 idempotency conflict; 429 rate limit; duplicate idempotency key returns the original result), GET /api/searches (200 or 401/429), GET /api/searches/:id (200; 400 malformed ID; 401 unauthenticated; 404 foreign/missing; 429), POST /api/searches/:id/cancel (200; 400/401/403/404/429; no cross-owner effect), GET export (200; 400/401/404/409/429), GET events (SSE 200; 400/401/404/429; owner-scoped replay); GET /api/resumes (200 or 401; no route-specific 429), POST resume (202; 400/401/403/409/413/429/503/507 with no partial publication), GET resume/:id (200; 400/401/404/503), recover/cancel (200; 400/401/403/404/409/429/503/507), DELETE resume (204; 400/401/403/409/429/503); GET /api/preparation (200/401/429), POST preparation/:checkId/ai-elaborate (200; 400/401/403/404/429/502/503/504 and no resume/contact/compensation data); POST /api/account/sessions/revoke-others and POST /api/account/password each return 204 on success, 400 for validation, 401 for unauthenticated, 403 for Origin/CSRF failure and 429 when rate-limited; revoke-others invalidates every other session while preserving the current session, and password change clears the current session after the credential update. Unsupported/disabled routes assert their documented 404/405/503 and no side effect. For NOT_APPLICABLE design-only rows assert no invented API call or success state.
CS-108-AC2.assertion: The acceptance matrix uses route/method-specific status, error and before/after side-effect assertions from the frozen full route/client contract table; it fails when implementation diverges, documentation omits a registered route, or a runtime row lacks a table entry. UI visibility never changes authorization.
CS-108-AC2.expectedResult: No cross-owner data, fabricated success or unauthorized capability is exposed; all failures remain observable and redacted.

CS-108-AC2.testFileOrProcedureId: PLANNED:apps/api/tests/visual-acceptance-contract.security.test.ts::visual acceptance fixtures preserve server authorization and failure semantics

CS-2-AC1.reviewer: Frontend, UX and QA; Release reviewer for hosted evidence

CS-2-AC1.setup: Create isolated synthetic owner data with one saved lead; launch the current Next.js app and scripts/check-ui.ts browser harness; set viewport to exactly 768 by 900 CSS pixels; capture browser name/version, window.innerWidth, target selector identity, element bounding box and computed expected geometry. Do not use real account data or historical removed source files as runtime fixtures.
CS-2-AC1.procedure: Run within the canonical integration CI environment: PostgreSQL with migrations, Redis, LocalStack SQS, built files worker/domain packages, production Next.js build/server and the isolated temporary test database created by scripts/check-ui.ts. In Linux WebKit, navigate to /saved and wait for the saved-workspace heading and the single UX-approved target element. Measure its actual geometry and the reference-derived expected position using the approved design contract. Chromium and Firefox remain suite-level controls at their existing configured viewports; the 768px defect assertion is WebKit-specific. Preserve the separate 390px row-stacking check as a distinct assertion and result.
CS-2-AC1.assertion: For Linux WebKit only, the target exists exactly once; window.innerWidth is 768; actual and approved expected geometry are both finite; the measured offset equals the approved expected offset within only the pre-approved tolerance. Before-fix evidence must demonstrate the ticket's specific 768px mismatch to call the defect reproduced. If the current surface has no target or no approved expected geometry, the test fails closed as unresolved and cannot report CS-2 accepted. The 390px overlap result cannot satisfy this assertion.
CS-2-AC1.expectedResult: A real current-surface 768px Linux-WebKit defect is either demonstrated with exact geometry for root-cause correction or explicitly reported as not reproduced; no inference from Windows or another viewport is accepted.
CS-2-AC1.testName: CS-2 Linux WebKit reproduces the approved saved-workspace 768px header geometry
CS-2-AC1.fixtures: Existing isolated check-ui owner fixture and one synthetic saved lead; approved UX target/geometry; no real credentials, resume data, external posting navigation or production services.
CS-2-AC1.negativeCase: Wrong viewport, missing/duplicate target, missing expected geometry, non-finite measurement, unapproved tolerance, wrong engine, no before-fix reproduction, or substituting the historical 390px overlap must fail as NOT_ACCEPTED; a healthy geometry positive control passes only at the approved expected offset.
CS-2-AC1.evidenceArtifact: Future redacted Playwright trace/result with exact commit, WebKit version, 768x900 CSS viewport, target identity, measured/expected geometry, approved tolerance and distinct 390px control result; no such current run is claimed.

CS-2-AC2.preconditions: The target defect and approved target geometry for AC1 are established; the exact assertion is checked into scripts/check-ui.ts before any implementation change.
CS-2-AC2.setup: Capture the failing pre-fix assertion from Linux WebKit at 768px and the separate 390px row-overlap control. Preserve the same fixture, selector, browser image, viewport, expected value and tolerance for before/after runs.
CS-2-AC2.procedure: Trace the failing 768px geometry to the responsible current layout rule/component; record a causal explanation referencing the measured values and source path. Make the smallest correction and run the identical browser procedure against the fixed revision without editing its assertion, selector, viewport or tolerance.
CS-2-AC2.assertion: The review artifact names a concrete source-level cause supported by the before-fix trace and shows the unchanged assertion failing before and passing after the fix. A change that only changes expected value, selector, viewport, timeout, retry count or tolerance does not pass. A cause for the historical 390px WebKit race is not a root cause for the 768px ticket unless separate evidence demonstrates the same mechanism at the approved 768px target.
CS-2-AC2.expectedResult: The 768px cause and correction are causally supported, and the exact assertion is unchanged across failing and passing revisions.
CS-2-AC2.testName: CS-2 root-cause fix passes the unchanged 768px browser assertion
CS-2-AC2.fixtures: Same synthetic owner/lead fixture and pinned browser environment as CS-2-AC1; source diff and redacted before/after traces.
CS-2-AC2.negativeCase: If no 768px failure can be demonstrated, no root cause can be claimed and the ticket remains unaccepted; assertion widening, 390px-only proof or unrelated CSS change fails review.
CS-2-AC2.evidenceArtifact: Future independent code/test review containing before/after assertion identity or hash, root-cause source references and both viewport outcomes.

CS-40.section: CS-40 / CS-88 — admin authorization and admin UX
CS-40.decision: Dedicated privileged Admin Control Plane with server-enforced RBAC, least privilege, seven approved roles and no arbitrary database editor or secret-bearing UI.
CS-40.remainingGate: Exact permission/projection contracts and independent security/design review. Approval does not prove implementation or authorize unrestricted mutations.

CS-44.decision: No second bespoke email-token recovery system. Carry non-enumeration, expiry, single-use, replay rejection and abuse controls into Cognito; preserve authenticated password change/operator recovery until release.
CS-44.remainingGate: Sender identity/domain evidence and security review; historical registration-disabled AC is the pre-Cognito safety boundary, not a ban on approved Cognito signup.

CS-46.decision: Explicit durable per-fact exclusion gate. Accepted resume facts plus explicit preferences only. Excluded facts contribute zero; reparse creates reviewable proposals without silently clearing candidate intent. Restoration explicit/reversible; provenance visible; explicit user years wins; no LLM reintroduction.
CS-46.remainingGate: Implementation/data contract and tests remain unproven. Historical AC2 'until re-parsed' is a lower bound, not permission to clear exclusions on reparse; later owner direction governs.

CS-88.section: CS-40 / CS-88 — admin authorization and admin UX
CS-88.decision: Admin Control Plane scope approved; imported Design System is visual authority; real redacted API data or honest unavailable states only.
CS-88.remainingGate: Exact per-screen responsive mappings, RBAC/API contracts and actual named independent reviews. Functional approval is not proof every screen is designed.

CS-89.decision: Assistive preparation/explanation approved but production default-OFF; never control deterministic ranking, authorization, identity, verification or application state.
CS-89.remainingGate: Runtime secret, current provider-catalog free-model proof, budget/kill switch, exact-SHA live verification and rollback remain required; no activation in this phase.

CS-90.decision: ap-south-1; verified normalized case-insensitive email; phone optional contact with phone OTP later; server provider exchange into opaque CareerScope session; auth.careerscope.tech after DNS/TLS; controlled owner linking without hash export; flagged canary with Argon2 rollback.
